clue.text: Composer's pen

definitions.meaning: a pen is an enclosure for animals, a coop or hutch

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side: the surname of the composer of 4'33", and an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the American composer John Cage, and a barred enclosure for confining animals.

clue.text: Surge regularly times a hundred coming up to speed, reaching virtual capacity

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means these pieces are read from bottom to top
regularly picks every other letter of the word Surge, its first, third and fifth

parts.note: by means times, as in multiplying six by two
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
pace means speed, rate of movement

explanation.surface: An electrical surge multiplies in a network until it hits the limit of some virtual system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes SRE from Surge; with BY and C, 'coming up' turns the lot to CYBERS. 'reaching' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the notional realm of computer networks, a virtual space or room in which online activity takes place.

clue.text: Setter's fiction elevated in spirit

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for spirit

parts.note: gin is a spirit, the distilled drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevated means the word is lifted, read upwards

parts.note: a tale is a piece of fiction, a story

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler's invented story gets raised up while they drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword setter, but it is the definition: something that makes jellies set. 'elevated' turns the story upwards, giving ELAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is a setting agent used to make jellies firm, so it is literally a thing that sets.

clue.text: Stirring pap, Roman official holds a spatula

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so the letters of pap are rearranged
holds means the official's title contains the next letter

parts.note: a lictor was an attendant officer in ancient Rome who carried the fasces

explanation.surface: A Roman official stirs baby food while wielding a spatula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' rearranges PAP to APP; LICTOR, an ancient Roman magistrate's attendant, 'holds' A to give LICATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is one kind of applicator, a flat tool for spreading ointment or paste onto a surface.

clue.text: Etiquette unpolitic, strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of unpolitic appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Bad manners are described as impolitic in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges UNPOLITIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctilio is a fine point of etiquette or a strict observance of formal conduct.

clue.text: Machine no longer functioning round hospital

indicators.note: round says the word for not functioning goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: late means dead, no longer alive or working
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A machine that has broken down is found around the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: LATE, as in 'the late king', goes 'round' H.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a workshop machine that spins a piece of wood or metal against a cutting tool.

clue.text: Iran recruits a lunatic in preliminary action

indicators.note: lunatic means wildly crazy, so the letters of Iran recruits a are jumbled

explanation.surface: Iran enlists a madman as an opening move before some conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunatic' rearranges IRAN RECRUITS A; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is a short play before the main one, hence any preliminary event or opening move.

clue.text: Cry before killing friend in lap of god almost

indicators.note: in the lap of means sitting within, so the friend sits inside the trimmed god
almost says the god's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A war cry before battle is spoken by a friend nestled in a god's lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves THO from the Norse god, and 'in lap of' seats the friend within it. The definition is a hunting cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunters cry tally-ho when the fox is sighted, the call that comes before the chase and kill.

clue.text: Biblical character's gospel unopened

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: gospel means the absolute truth, as in taking something as gospel

explanation.surface: A figure from the Bible has a gospel that has never been opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gospel' suggests a book of the Bible, but here it means TRUTH; 'unopened' drops the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is the Moabite woman whose story is told in the Old Testament book named after her.

clue.text: Prime minister unlocked success?

parts.note: unlocked read as without locks of hair, that is bald
a win is a success or victory

explanation.surface: A head of government breaks through a lock and wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlocked' means without locks of hair. Stanley Baldwin was British Prime Minister three times between 1923 and 1937.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin was a Conservative leader who served as British Prime Minister in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Wallower almost breaking limb bearing into crowd? Beat it

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into the middle of the word for limb

parts.note: a wing is a limb of a bird

indicators.note: almost says the wallowing animal's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the hippo, short for hippopotamus, wallows in mud and water

indicators.note: into puts the compass bearing inside the word for crowd

parts.note: to cram is to crowd, pack tightly together
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A huge beast, wallowing, crashes in and charges into the crowd, so run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat it' reads as 'go away', but it is an instruction: this is what you beat. The wallower is the hippopotamus, and 'almost' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipping cream is cream rich enough to be beaten until thick, so 'beat it' tells you what to do with it.

clue.text: Surprise, no starter —— time for little cake

indicators.note: no starter means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to startle is to surprise or alarm

explanation.surface: A small cake is a surprise even though there was no first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starter' drops the S from STARTLE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a small tart, a little pastry case with a sweet filling, so a small cake.

clue.text: Shopping taking the blame in distortion of reality

indicators.note: in places the phrase inside the jumbled word
a distortion twists something out of shape, so the letters of reality are rearranged

parts.note: the rap is blame or punishment, as in taking the rap

explanation.surface: Someone shopping takes the blame for a warped view of reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distortion of' rearranges REALITY to RETAILY; THE RAP goes 'in' it. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail therapy is shopping done to cheer oneself up, buying things as a pick-me-up.

clue.text: Parting note thanked originally at old fashioned length

indicators.note: originally suggests the letters of thanked made something else in an earlier form

parts.note: the ell is an obsolete measure of length, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: A farewell letter thanks someone in an old-fashioned manner, at some length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges THANKED; the ELL was an old English measure of cloth. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A death knell is the bell tolled at someone's death, a sound marking their final departure.

clue.text: Sanctimonious joke about beautiful person

parts.note: pi is informal for sanctimonious, piously self-righteous

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for joke is read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: A self-righteous person's joke is about someone good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is a British informal word for smugly pious; PUN turned 'about' gives NUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is an attractive person whose picture is pinned up on a wall by admirers.

clue.text: Two short limbs to negotiate tempestuous conditions not on for swimmer

indicators.note: to negotiate means to go round an obstacle, so the limbs surround the stormy weather
two means the shortened limb is taken twice
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a leg is a limb

indicators.note: not on means the letters of the word on are removed

parts.note: a monsoon brings stormy, rainy weather

explanation.surface: A swimmer with two stumpy legs struggles through a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the final letter of each limb and 'Two' doubles it; 'not on' leaves MONSO; 'to negotiate' has the limbs go round it. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The lemon sole is a flatfish found in European waters, so it is a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Process food in wine cape in China

indicators.note: the second in puts the wine and cape inside the word for china

parts.note: china means mate, from Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate'
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: Eating in China involves wine served on a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, a friend. ASTI and C go 'in' MATE; the first 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To masticate is to chew, the first stage in processing food in the mouth.

clue.text: Skinny? Back at university, gaining ounces getting drunk

indicators.note: gaining means the scrambled word takes the turned pair inside it
getting drunk means becoming muddled, so the letters of ounces are rearranged
back means the following words are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: Someone thin is back at college, putting on weight because they are drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' looks like 'thin', but here it means 'of the skin'. 'Back' gives UTA; 'getting drunk' gives CNEOUS, and 'gaining' takes UTA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutaneous means relating to the skin, so it is skinny in a jokey literal sense.

clue.text: Touchy and spiteful woman lifted hat

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means the word is raised, read upwards

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful or malicious woman
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A sensitive, catty woman whips off a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touchy' suggests irritable, but it means 'of touch'. CAT, 'lifted', gives TAC; TILE is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of touch, so touchy in a literal sense.

clue.text: Unlimited jargon by thieves, primarily?

indicators.note: unlimited means without its limits, so the word loses its first and last letters
primarily picks out the first letter of thieves

explanation.surface: Thieves' slang is used without restriction, chiefly among criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' takes the middle of JARGON, ARGO; 'primarily' adds T. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the secret slang of a group, originally that of thieves and criminals.

clue.text: Is it a hot surface? Good question!

parts.note: a riddle is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something is a hotplate, and is praised for asking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is it a' and the closing 'Good question' make a quiz: G plus RIDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is a flat iron plate heated for cooking, so a hot cooking surface.

clue.text: Bird follows insect, one passing through bit of Leicester, perhaps?

definitions.text: one passing through bit of Leicester, perhaps?

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
tails means follows, as a detective tails a suspect
a tick is a small bloodsucking creature, loosely called an insect

explanation.surface: A bird chases an insect, and something pierces a piece of Leicester city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leicester' looks like the city, but it is Red Leicester, a British cheese; a cube of it is often speared on a stick at parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail stick is a small pointed stick used to spear party nibbles such as cubes of cheese.

clue.text: End of boot used in beating up teach

indicators.note: used in means the letter is put inside the turned word
in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rout is a beating, a heavy defeat

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of boot

explanation.surface: A teacher uses the toe of a boot when giving a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUT read 'up' gives TUOR; T goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to teach, especially a single pupil or a small group.

clue.text: Is it above the ankle? A little lower

definitions.meaning: the fleshy back of the lower leg sits just above the ankle
a lower is something that lows or moos, a cow, so a little one is a young cow

explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as 'further down', but it is something that lows: a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both fit: the muscle at the back of the shin, and a young bovine animal.

clue.text: Insect eats fruit for food

indicators.note: eats means the insect takes the fruit inside it

parts.note: an ant is an insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: An insect feeds on a piece of fruit as its meal.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT 'eats' LIME; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment.

clue.text: A card game requiring cut

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A card game in which the pack has to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like part of the card game, but it is the definition: shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut or shorten it while keeping its sense.

clue.text: Early boat, among all the rest, that has many cheap offers

indicators.note: among puts the early boat inside the group of the others

parts.note: the rest of the boats taken together make a fleet
AM, ante meridiem, means in the early part of the day
an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: An ancient ship sits among all the others as bargains are offered.
explanation.walkthrough: AM ARK goes 'among' FLEET; 'all the rest' means the other boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is a street market selling cheap second-hand goods, a place with many bargains.

clue.text: Fine water source

definitions.meaning: fine means in good health, all right
a shaft sunk into the ground to draw up water

explanation.definitionFit: Both fit: being in good health, and a shaft dug to reach groundwater.
